title: External components of the earth
competency: State the four components of the Earth and how they constantly interact.

keywords.def: The solid, rocky part of the Earth's surface.
All the water on Earth: oceans, seas, lakes, rivers, ice and water vapour.
The part of the Earth where living things exist.
The envelope of air around the Earth.
The four parts (subsystems) of the Earth's environment: lithosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere and atmosphere.

ideas.name: The four components of the Earth

en.text: The Earth's surface has four parts. The lithosphere is land and rock. The hydrosphere is all the water. The biosphere is where living things exist. The atmosphere is the air. Air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen. Oceans cover about 71% of the surface and hold about 97% of the water.

am.text: የመሬት ገጽ አራት ክፍሎች አሉት። ሊቶስፌር የየብስና የአለት ክፍል ነው። ሃይድሮስፌር ሁሉም ውሃ ነው። ባዮስፌር ሕያዋን ፍጥረታት የሚኖሩበት ክፍል ነው። ከባቢ አየር አየሩ ነው። አየር 78% ናይትሮጅንና 21% ኦክስጅን ነው። ውቅያኖሶች 71% የመሬትን ገጽ ይሸፍናሉ፤ 97% ውሃንም ይይዛሉ።

screens.title: Land, water, life, air
screens.text: Think of Ras Dejen, Lake Tana, a teff plant and the air you breathe.
screens.ask: How many main parts does the Earth's outer environment have? Guess.
screens.after: The book names four: land, water, living things and air. Read about each one.

screens.title: A. The lithosphere
paras: The Earth's physical environment has four components, or subsystems.
The lithosphere is the solid, rocky part of the Earth. It is the coolest and most rigid part.
Its surface is very uneven. It has mountains, plateaus, plains and valleys.
In Ethiopia it reaches from Ras Dejen (Ras Dashen), the highest peak, down to Dallol. Dallol is about 116 m below sea level.
screens.note: The book gives Ras Dejen's height as 4,620 m. Newer measurements give about 4,550 m.

screens.title: B. The hydrosphere
paras: The hydrosphere is all the water on Earth. It is found as liquid, ice and water vapour.
It is in oceans, seas, lakes and rivers.
Oceans are its biggest part. They cover about 71% of the Earth's surface. They hold about 97% of its water.

screens.title: Land and water spheres
defs: The solid, rocky part of the Earth's surface. From Greek lithos, stone.
All the water on Earth: oceans, seas, lakes, rivers, ice and water vapour. From Greek hydro, water.

screens.title: Oceans and water
screens.text: Oceans hold about how much of Earth's water?
screens.why: Oceans hold 97% of the water and cover about 71% of the surface.
screens.clue: Two numbers are given: one for surface, one for water.

screens.title: C. The biosphere
paras: The biosphere is the part of the Earth where living things exist.
It is a zone near the surface. It reaches from the ocean floor up several kilometres into the air.

screens.title: D. The atmosphere
paras: The atmosphere is the envelope of air around the Earth. It is a mixture of gases.
The most common gas is nitrogen (78%). It enters the air when volcanoes erupt. It also comes from dead plants and animals that decay.
Next is oxygen (21%), made mainly by plants. Together they are about 99% of the air.
The rest is argon, carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour.

screens.title: Life and air spheres
defs: The part of the Earth where living things exist. From Greek bio, life.
The envelope of air around the Earth. From Greek atmos, vapour.

screens.title: The main gas
screens.text: Which gas makes up most of the air?
screens.why: About 78% of the air is nitrogen; oxygen is about 21%.
screens.clue: Look at the biggest number in the table.

screens.title: Where oxygen comes from
screens.text: Oxygen is the second most common gas in the air.
screens.ask: Oxygen in the air is made mainly by ___.
screens.why: Plants make most of the oxygen in the air.
screens.clue: Which living things make their own food in sunlight?

screens.title: Sort it
screens.text: Which sphere does each thing belong to?
items: It is a gas in the air.
It is the main gas in the air.
screens.why: Land and rock: lithosphere. Water: hydrosphere. Living things: biosphere. Air: atmosphere.
screens.clue: Ask: is it rock, water, alive, or a gas?
screens.worked: Ras Dejen is rock, so lithosphere. River and Lake Tana are water, so hydrosphere. Eagle and teff are alive, so biosphere. Oxygen and nitrogen are gases, so atmosphere.

en.text: The four spheres are closely connected. Birds fly through the air. Water flows through soil. People breathe air, drink water and walk on the ground. We could not live without any of the four. People build dams from rock and use flowing water to make electricity.

am.text: አራቱ ክፍሎች በቅርብ የተሳሰሩ ናቸው። ወፎች በአየር ውስጥ ይበራሉ። ውሃ በአፈር ውስጥ ይፈሳል። ሰዎች አየር ይተነፍሳሉ፣ ውሃ ይጠጣሉ፣ በመሬት ላይ ይራመዳሉ። ያለ አራቱ መኖር አንችልም። ሰዎች ከአለት ግድብ ይገነባሉ፤ በሚፈስ ውሃ ኤሌክትሪክ ያመነጫሉ።

screens.title: Cold on the mountain
screens.text: The top of Ras Dejen is much colder than a valley below it.
screens.ask: Why do you think high mountains are colder? Guess.
opts: They are closer to the Sun
The air is thinner and there is more rain and snow
screens.after: Land meets thin air and more precipitation up high. Plants and animals adapt. The spheres work together.

screens.title: How do the Earth's spheres interact?
paras: The four spheres are closely connected. Their interaction shapes every environment.
High mountains are colder than valleys. There the lithosphere meets thinner air and more precipitation. This makes a cool or icy climate. Plants and animals have adapted to it.
Birds (biosphere) fly through the air (atmosphere). Water (hydrosphere) flows through soil (lithosphere).
People breathe air, drink water and walk on the ground. We could not live without any of the four.
People build dams from rock. They use flowing water to spin turbines that make electricity.

screens.title: Four parts, one system
defs: The four parts (subsystems) of the Earth's environment: lithosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere and atmosphere. They constantly interact.

screens.title: Building a dam
screens.text: People build a dam from rock. Which two spheres are interacting?
screens.why: People are part of the biosphere; rock is the lithosphere.
screens.clue: Which sphere are people in? Which is rock in?

screens.title: Water and land
screens.text: Which example shows the hydrosphere and lithosphere interacting?
screens.clue: Find the example with water in it.

screens.title: Birds in the sky
screens.text: A bird flies over Lake Tana.
screens.ask: The bird is part of the biosphere. The air it flies through is the ___.
screens.clue: Which sphere is the envelope of air?

screens.title: Power from a river
screens.text: At a dam on the Abay (Blue Nile), flowing water spins turbines. They make electricity for homes in Ethiopia.
screens.ask: Which sphere is the flowing water?
screens.why: All water on Earth, including rivers, is the hydrosphere.
screens.clue: Hydro comes from the Greek word for what?

screens.title: Could we live without one?
screens.text: People could live well without the lithosphere.
screens.why: We walk on the ground and need it. We could not live without any of the four spheres.
screens.clue: Think about where you stand and grow food.

test.title: Spheres
test.text: Match each sphere to what it contains.
test.why: Lithos = stone, hydro = water, bio = life, atmos = vapour.

test.ask: Oceans cover about ___% of the Earth's surface.
test.why: They also hold about 97% of Earth's water.

test.text: Oxygen is the most common gas in the air.
test.why: Nitrogen is about 78% of the air. Oxygen is about 21%.

notes.text: The book gives Ras Dejen's height as 4,620 m. Newer measurements give about 4,550 m.
The external-components group tasks ('Things to do') are open-ended and are not turned into graded items. The 'Sort it' figure is used as a practise item.
The Abay dam practise item and the oxygen blank are added examples built on the book's statements (dams and turbines; oxygen made mainly by plants).

screens.title: Name the sphere
screens.text: Ask one question about the thing.
steps: Is it rock or land? Lithosphere.
Is it water, ice or vapour? Hydrosphere.
Is it air or a gas? Atmosphere.

screens.title: Your turn
screens.text: Lake Tana belongs to which sphere?
screens.why: A lake is water, so it is part of the hydrosphere.
screens.clue: Is a lake rock, water, alive or air?
